word: I felt that I had let the previous generation of entrepreneurs down, that I had dropped the baton as it was being passed to me.
meaning: 我覺得自己讓上一代的企業家們失望了，就像是在接力棒傳到我手上的那一刻，我把它掉了。
example: He felt like he had failed the people who came before him, like a runner dropping the relay baton.
hint:
中文解釋：用接力賽的比喻，形容自己的失敗讓整個創業傳承中斷，充滿愧疚感。
1) let...down (phr.): 讓…失望；syn: disappointed; ant: made proud
2) dropped the baton (phr.): 掉了接力棒（比喻搞砸了交接）；syn: failed the handoff; ant: carried on
pronunciation: Guilt: I FELT | I had LET them DOWN | DROPPED the BA-ton | as it was be-ing PASSED to ME.

word: I met with David Packard and Bob Noyce, and tried to apologize for screwing up so badly.
meaning: 我去見了大衛·帕卡德和鮑勃·諾伊斯，試著為自己搞砸一切而道歉。
example: He visited two legendary tech founders to personally apologize for his failures.
hint:
中文解釋：David Packard（HP 創辦人）和 Bob Noyce（英特爾創辦人）都是科技業前輩——Jobs 向他們道歉，顯示當時的深刻羞愧。
1) apologize (v.): 道歉；syn: say sorry; ant: defend oneself
2) screwing up (phr.): 搞砸、犯嚴重錯誤；syn: messing up; ant: succeeding
pronunciation: Humble: I MET with DAV-id PACK-ard and BOB NOYCE | tried to a-POL-o-gize | for SCREW-ing UP so BAD-ly.

word: I was a very public failure, and I even thought about running away from the Valley.
meaning: 我是一個非常公開的失敗者，我甚至想過逃離矽谷。
example: His failure was visible to everyone, and he seriously considered leaving Silicon Valley.
hint:
中文解釋：誠實面對自己的脆弱——「逃離矽谷」這個念頭顯示出他當時有多低落。
1) public failure (n.): 公開的失敗；syn: visible setback; ant: private struggle
2) running away (phr.): 逃跑、逃離；syn: fleeing; ant: facing it
pronunciation: Vulnerable: a VER-y PUB-lic FAIL-ure | e-ven THOUGHT | a-bout RUN-ning a-WAY from the VAL-ley.

word: But something slowly began to dawn on me: I still loved what I did.
meaning: 但有一件事開始慢慢浮現在我的意識中：我依然熱愛我所做的事。
example: Gradually, he realized something important: his passion for the work had not disappeared.
hint:
中文解釋：轉折的關鍵時刻——「dawn on me」是頓悟的開始，熱愛讓他找到繼續走下去的理由。
1) dawn on (phr.): 逐漸明白、頓悟；syn: occur to; ant: remain unaware
2) still loved (phr.): 依然熱愛；syn: still passionate; ant: had stopped caring
pronunciation: Turning point: some-thing SLOW-ly be-GAN to DAWN on me | I STILL LOVED | what I DID.

word: The turn of events at Apple had not changed that one bit.
meaning: 蘋果公司發生的一切，絲毫沒有改變這一點。
example: Despite everything that happened at Apple, his love for the work remained unchanged.
hint:
中文解釋：強調熱情的韌性——外在的失敗、羞辱，都無法澆熄內心的熱愛。
1) turn of events (n.): 事情的轉變；syn: what happened; ant: (n/a)
2) not one bit (phr.): 絲毫沒有；syn: not at all; ant: completely
pronunciation: Firm: the TURN of e-VENTS at AP-ple | had NOT changed that | ONE BIT.

word: I'd been rejected, but I was still in love.
meaning: 我被拒絕了，但我依然愛著它。
example: He had been pushed out, yet his passion for the work he loved remained strong.
hint:
中文解釋：用「still in love」比喻對工作的熱情——被趕走了，但心沒有離開。
1) rejected (v.): 被拒絕、被排斥；syn: turned away; ant: accepted
2) still in love (phr.): 依然愛著；syn: still passionate; ant: had given up
pronunciation: Honest: I'd been re-JECT-ed | but I was STILL in LOVE. (slight pause before 'but')

word: And so I decided to start over.
example: With that realization, he made the decision to begin again from scratch.
hint:
中文解釋：短而有力的行動宣言——放下舊包袱，重新出發。
1) decided (v.): 決定；syn: chose; ant: gave up
2) start over (phr.): 重新開始；syn: begin again; ant: stay stuck
pronunciation: Clean break: And so I de-CI-ded | to START O-ver. (pause before 'start over')

word: I didn't see it then, but it turned out that getting fired from Apple was the best thing that could have ever happened to me.
meaning: 當時我看不清，但後來證明，被蘋果解雇是我人生中可能發生過最好的事。
example: In hindsight, being fired from Apple turned out to be an unexpected blessing.
hint:
中文解釋：人生重要的反轉——最壞的打擊，後來成為最好的禮物，呼應「connecting the dots」的主題。
1) turned out (phr.): 結果（出乎意料地）；syn: proved to be; ant: was expected to be
2) best thing (phr.): 最好的事；syn: greatest blessing; ant: worst thing
pronunciation: Revelation: I did-n't SEE it THEN | but it TURNED OUT | get-ting FIRED from AP-ple | was the BEST THING.
